The Princely Abbey of Corvey (German: Fürststift Corvey or Fürstabtei Corvey) is a former Benedictine abbey and ecclesiastical principality in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Originally built in 822 and 885 and remodelled in the Baroque period, the abbey is an exceptional example of Carolingian architecture, the oldest surviving example of a westwork, and the oldest standing medieval structure in Westphalia. title: Corvey UNESCO World Heritage Site - Deutsche Märchenstraße
content: UNESCO World Heritage Site Corvey - A legacy of humanity at the gates of Höxter. The former Benedictine abbey of Corvey was founded in 822 by order of Charlemagne and is considered one of the most important monasteries in medieval Germany. The early medieval westwork of the abbey church is visible from afar. It forms the visible core of the World Heritage Site and, together with the baroque monastery building and the extensive princely library, fascinates guests from all over the world. The **Westwork** of the baroque abbey church of Corvey is 1,200 years old and one of the few buildings from the time of Charlemagne that has been preserved in its essential parts. The original vaulted hall with columns and pillars on the first floor and the main room on the upper floor make Corvey one of the most striking examples of the so-called "Carolingian Renaissance". The grave of the Corvey librarian and poet of the German national anthem, Hoffmann von Fallersleben, is located in the adjacent cemetery.

UNESCO World Heritage Site: the Imperial Abbey of Corvey 
			- Germany Travel
content: # The Imperial Abbey of Corvey – world culture and cultural hub in the Weser Uplands. The Imperial Abbey of Corvey is more than a UNESCO World Heritage Site: it embodies world culture. Nowadays, Corvey is a privately owned cultural gem in the Weser Uplands. And it is still a place of pilgrimage on the long road to Santiago de Compostela. Even the first abbey, founded around 822, was a spiritual, cultural and economic hub and a major driving force behind Christianisation in Europe. As imperial and prince-abbots and then as price-bishops, the clergy at Corvey had just as much political influence in the Kingdom of Germany within the Holy Roman Empire as the global princes of the 19th century later did. As do the Imperial Hall, which was built when the prince-abbots were in power, and the Princely Library with its 74,000 books dating back to the late 18th and early 19th century.
